findings.title: GBJ half-cycle diode allocation is reversed
findings.why_it_matters: The four-diode model assigns each half-cycle's 40 W share to the non-conducting diode pair. The PFC adapter injects positive line-sign current out of bridge.2 (AC1) and into bridge.3 (AC2), so the positive half-cycle conducts AC2-to-plus and minus-to-AC1 (indices [1, 2]); this code selects [0, 3] instead. Any asymmetric half-cycle waveform therefore produces wrong per-junction temperatures and lead coupling, while the current symmetric fixture hides the swap by yielding 10 W per diode.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the pair mapping from the reviewed GBJ pin map and swap the branches to positive line-sign => [1, 2] and negative line-sign => [0, 3]; add an asymmetric waveform test that asserts the resulting four diode powers.

findings.title: Fan-loss FEM case is omitted from harness findings
findings.why_it_matters: GBJ assessment generation adds a dedicated fan-loss sensitivity, but the mandatory harness only extracts nominal-fine and weak-assembly cases. Consequently no cooling rule reports or evaluates the fan-loss result; a changed or over-limit fan-loss case can still replay successfully without changing any emitted cooling finding. Selecting the fan-loss case and emitting its result as an explicit sensitivity/INDETERMINATE finding keeps the computed evidence visible and reviewable.
findings.suggested_fix: Require named("fan-loss") in run_gbj_model and include its package and whole-joint peaks in a dedicated cooling finding, keeping applicability INDETERMINATE because shutdown timing and installed airflow remain unverified.
evidence: zapote/packages/zapote-harness/src/bridge_thermal.rs:96-97 -- let nominal = named("nominal-fine")?; / let weak = named("weak-assembly")?;
zapote/packages/zapote-harness/src/bridge_thermal.rs:148-165 -- budget_finding and pcb use nominal, while weak_finding uses weak; no fan-loss case is selected or evaluated

residual_risks: The GBJ fallback keeps AC2 at full terminal RMS when no determined cut exists, so the FEM load remains a sensitivity rather than a resolved pad/contact current distribution.
The package network, lead paths, sink boundary, and installed airflow remain model assumptions; numerical replay does not qualify those physical paths or hardware ratings.
testing_gaps: No asymmetric line-sign waveform test catches the reversed GBJ diode pair mapping; the current symmetric fixture makes both mappings produce equal diode powers.
No harness test asserts that the fan-loss scenario is selected and represented in a mandatory cooling finding.
